transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Omar Reyes (Redwood SE), Sarah Mitchell (CTO - Horizon), Rahul Desai (ML Eng), Maya Chen (Infra)

Summary: Quick discovery focused on model selection for multi-lingual customer support and internal doc Q&A. Main constraints: need 32k context for long docs, multilingual model support (en+es+fr), desire for tool-calling (knowledge base enrichment + DB lookups), and clear security controls (VPC, KMS). Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs and asked for perf/cost comparisons and security docs. Agreed next steps at end.

[00:00] Lena: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh this is Lena from Redwood, i'm joined by Omar on the SE side, how are you all?
[00:10] Sarah: good hey, thanks for squeezing us in, i'm Sarah, CTO at Horizon. we have Rahul and Maya on the line.
[00:18] Omar: hi all, quick agenda - understand your workloads, context length needs, multilingual, tool-calling, and security constraints; then we'll talk about hosting/deployment options and recommend models. sound good?
[00:28] Rahul: yep that's perfect. to start, our primary use case is a support assistant that can ingest long policy docs and past ticket threads, so we need long context. also multi-lingual for en/es/fr.
[00:40] Maya: and from infra we need to understand network/topology - we are planning to keep PII inside our VPC and need KMS integration.
[00:48] Lena: great, that helps. can you quantify "long" for context? are we talking 8k, 32k, more?
[00:55] Rahul: ideally 32k. some of our compliance docs are long, and we also want a session-level memory for multi-turn tickets.
[01:05] Omar: okay, good. on the model side we typically recommend comparing a few open model families. for 32k you can look at long-context variants like Mistral Long or the Redcloud-style 32k derivatives - sorry that was my lazy transcription, i mean Redwood-curated 32k variants - they have tradeoffs on latency and cost.
[01:25] Sarah: quick question on tool calling: we want the assistant to do KB lookups, and call an internal function to fetch customer metadata. is that supported with the hosted API or do we need Dedicated/Private?
[01:36] Omar: tool-calling is supported in hosted, yes; you can do function-style calls. the difference is around data residency and network access. if your function endpoints need to live inside a VPC with no public ingress, that's where Private or Dedicated with VPC peering comes in. hosted can do secure integrations but for strict egress controls Private is typical.
[01:55] Maya: we have a policy that PII must never traverse public endpoints. we prefer a private deployment but are open if dedicated can meet the egress/KMS needs.
[02:05] Lena: understood. Dedicated gives reserved capacity with VPC options and can be configured for private connectivity, but Private (on-prem or customer VPC) gives you full control. Pricing and ops differ, so we'll send a comparison.
[02:18] Rahul: on model accuracy: we evaluated a few LLMs internally, OpenAI did well but cost is high. we want an open model that handles Spanish and French well - do you have benchmarks?
[02:28] Omar: yes, we have multilingual perf profiles. Mistral family has decent multilingual, some LLama-derivatives are patched for EU languages, and we also test Mistral and Llama-2/3 variants. caveat: smaller quantized models drop quality on rare languages. we'll share our perf sheet.
[02:46] Sarah: latency is a concern. for user-facing chat we want sub-800ms p50 on short queries; for long-doc search it's okay to be higher but cost matters.
[02:58] Omar: sub-800ms p50 is doable for hosted with optimized kernels on short sequences; for 32k it depends - latency bumps and you pay more compute. Dedicated can help with predictable tails. also caching common prefixes and KV caching helps.
[03:16] Rahul: can you explain KV cache vs prefix caching briefly?
[03:20] Omar: sure - prefix caching stores commonly repeated prefixes so you avoid re-computing tokens; KV cache is the transformer key/value cache for autoregressive decoding and helps with multi-turn context when reusing earlier token states. both reduce token compute but in different ways.
[03:36] Sarah: are there particular model families you recommend for tool-calling reliability? we've had models hallucinate function names or arguments before.
[03:45] Lena: yes, models that are trained or fine-tuned with instruction and function calling primitives tend to be better. we often recommend testing a couple: a higher-quality LLaMA-3 variant or Mistral-instruct style models for deterministic function output. Redwood also verifies model variants for structured outputs.
[04:02] Maya: security checklist - SOC2? audit logs? SSO?
[04:07] Lena: hosted has SOC2 + enterprise contracts; Dedicated/Private adds more controls: dedicated includes audit logs and can integrate with SAML SSO, Private supports your KMS/HSM and full network control. we'll attach our security pack.
[04:21] Rahul: perf testing - can you run a benchmark that mimics our load? we have lots of concurrent sessions, about 120 RPS peak, average message size small but context heavy.
[04:33] Omar: yes, we can run shortbench with your sample prompts. two asks - can you share a sample of typical threads (anonymized) and a target SLA for throughput/latency?
[04:44] Sarah: we'll share anonymized samples. SLA target - p95 under 2s for typical user queries, p50 under 800ms.
[04:53] Lena: perfect. also want to discuss cost - are you looking at usage-based hosted first or a reserved dedicated contract?
[05:01] Sarah: we'd prefer to pilot hosted to iterate quickly, but if cost for 32k becomes too high we may move to Dedicated. timeline is Q1 pilot, Q2 decision.
[05:10] Lena: that aligns with many customers. we can propose a pilot using hosted with a cost projection, and parallel work to size Dedicated if it makes sense.
[05:18] Rahul: about tokenization: our data includes lots of legal snippets; does tokenization dramatically change cost for long docs?
[05:26] Omar: yes, tokenization affects token count. for legal text you might see higher per-word tokenization; we recommend sample tokenization during bench. quantization profile also matters for Dedicated cost.
[05:37] Sarah: do you support model pinning and gradual rollouts?
[05:40] Lena: yes, Redwood supports model version pinning, canary and A/B rollouts, and automatic fallbacks to cheaper variants if errors spike.
[05:49] Maya: network-wise, what's the typical architecture for Dedicated with VPC? does traffic route through Redwood control plane?
[05:56] Omar: Dedicated offers a customer VPC with private peering; control plane is reachable via TLS but you can configure minimal egress. Private deployment removes our control plane from your network if you want full on-prem. we'll include a diagram.
[06:10] Rahul: competition wise, we looked at Anthropic and OpenAI endpoints; can Redwood match the developer experience? we need SDKs and streaming.
[06:20] Lena: yes, we have SDKs and streaming/responses, plus embeddings and reranking APIs. and a model catalog with verified perf.
[06:28] Sarah: any gotchas with multilingual consistency over long contexts? sometimes models drift or forget older parts of the doc.
[06:36] Omar: memory drift is a known issue. approaches: hierarchical retrieval, chunking + retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for very long docs, and using KV caches for session state. also evaluation on your prompt sets will show degradation patterns.
[06:57] Rahul: on-tool calling again - does Redwood enforce schema for tool outputs? we want strict JSON outputs for downstream processors.
[07:04] Omar: we recommend using function-calling or structured output enforcement with RL-style scoring; some models are better at strict JSON. Redwood can add post-processing validators and QA checks in the pipeline to reject malformed outputs.
[07:20] Sarah: curious about quantization - if we go with Dedicated and 8-bit quantized models, do you see major quality loss for legal language?
[07:30] Omar: slight drop, depends on model. some instruction-tuned models are robust to int8, but rare token performance can suffer. we can test a couple of quant profiles and share delta metrics.
[07:45] Maya: retention/retention policies - hosted stores logs for 30 days by default? we need 90 days for audit plus ability to purge.
[07:56] Lena: hosted default retention is shorter, enterprise tiers offer configurable retention and exportable logs. Dedicated/Private gives you retention control. we'll include that in the security doc.
[08:07] Rahul: if we want to test a 32k context model, what's the expected cost delta compared to 8k?
[08:14] Omar: roughly 2.5x-4x per-request compute depending on sequence lengths and batching efficiency. exact numbers depend on token distribution; we'll model using your samples.
[08:26] Sarah: can you share examples of customers who use 32k for doc Q&A?
[08:31] Lena: yep, we've worked with legaltech and enterprise support orgs - we'll anonymize case studies.
[08:38] [small cross talk] Rahul: (murmur) also need to check latency in eu-west region...
[08:45] Omar: we have regional endpoints and can provision Dedicated capacity in eu-west.
[08:50] Sarah: about SLA - do Dedicated contracts include latency SLAs or just uptime?
[08:55] Lena: primarily uptime SLAs; latency targets are part of the expected performance profile for reserved capacity, but we can include performance SLOs in enterprise deals.
[09:07] Maya: we will need KMS integration - does Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[09:12] Omar: yes, Dedicated and Private support KMS/HSM integration for key ownership; hosted supports envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys or enterprise KMS in some tiers.
[09:24] Rahul: ok, curious about evals - can you run accuracy evals on our labeled set in spanish and french?
[09:30] Lena: yes, we can run evals and tie regression alerts to your prompt sets. we'll need the dataset and labels.
[09:38] Sarah: any preliminary model recommendation for pilot?
[09:41] Omar: for pilot, try a Mistral-instruct 32k variant and a LLaMA-3 8/32k variant. run the higher-quality LLaMA-3 for critical flows and Mistral for faster throughput; we'll benchmark both.
[09:56] Rahul: that sounds good. also we have an internal vector DB for retrieval; does Redwood integrate with that or do we need to host embeddings externally?
[10:04] Omar: you can host embeddings yourself and call them, or use Redwood embeddings; integration is straightforward. for private setups you can keep vectors inside your VPC.
[10:14] Sarah: timeline recap - pilot in Q1, decision in Q2. what's the pilot scope?
[10:21] Lena: a 4-week pilot: integrate sample app, run bench, evaluate accuracy and cost. we'll propose pilot success criteria and deliverables.
[10:30] Maya: cost model - we'd like a projection for 6 months at our expected usage.
[10:34] Lena: we'll include a 6-month cost projection for hosted and a sizing estimate for Dedicated with reserved nodes.
[10:40] Rahul: any limitations on function-call latency when calling internal microservices?
[10:45] Omar: network hops add latency; in Private/Dedicated with VPC peering you can keep endpoints local which reduces RTT. we'll model that in bench.
[10:54] Sarah: okay can we get security docs and SOC2?
[10:58] Lena: yes; i'll attach security pack and SOC2 attestation.
[11:02] [silence, typing]
[11:20] Lena: quick recap of next steps - i'll send pricing and pilot proposal, Omar will run bench once you send sample prompts, and Maya will provide infra constraints.
[11:33] Sarah: perfect. one more small thing - do you support auto-fallback to cheaper model when errors spike?
[11:40] Omar: yes we have routing policies and automatic fallbacks to compatible variants.
[11:46] Rahul: great. that's all from us.
[11:50] Lena: thanks everyone! we'll follow up with docs and a proposed pilot plan.
[11:55] Sarah: thanks, bye.

End transcript.
